clips.text_zh: 十年前你揸一樣嘢，揀BTC定黃金？黃金老嘢穩陣啲，BTC就係digital gold。又係選擇題lol 我自己就All-in左prop firm。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: If you had to hold only one asset for the next 10 years, would you pick Bitcoin or gold? Gold is the old safe choice, while Bitcoin is often called digital gold. Anons on /biz/ are arguing about which one is better. /biz/ thread today.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread debating Bitcoin vs gold as a 10-year hold

signal.rationale: OP frames Bitcoin as a long-term hold versus gold, implicitly bullish on BTC over a 10-year horizon

clips.text_en_b2: If you were forced to hold a single asset for the next ten years, would you go with Bitcoin or gold? Gold remains the classic safe haven that has weathered countless storms, whereas Bitcoin is increasingly pitched as digital gold for the tech-savvy crowd. Anons over on /biz/ are once again tearing each other apart over which pick actually wins long-term. At the end of the day, I went all-in on a prop firm challenge instead and I am not looking back.
clips.text_en_c1: Were one compelled to allocate capital to a single asset for the coming decade, the perennial debate between Bitcoin and gold would resurface with renewed vigour. Gold, the time-honoured store of value, offers a provenance of stability stretching back millennia, whereas Bitcoin — frequently dubbed digital gold — promises asymmetric upside, albeit accompanied by profound volatility. The thread on /biz/ has, predictably, bifurcated into maximalists and goldbugs, each marshalling historical precedent and chartist conviction alike. Personally, I have eschewed the binary altogether, having committed my capital to a proprietary trading firm, where the firm's risk parameters govern my exposure rather than the vicissitudes of either market.
clips.text_en_c2: Forced to commit a single position for the coming decade, the perennial question resurfaces on /biz/: Bitcoin or gold? Gold, the venerable store of value refined over millennia, is widely regarded as the more conservative allocation, whereas Bitcoin, notwithstanding its volatility, has been elevated by its proponents to the status of digital gold—an asset whose scarcity is algorithmic rather than geological. The thread today devolves, predictably, into the familiar partisan skirmish between permabulls dismissing the yellow metal as a relic and goldbugs decrying crypto as a speculative fever dream. I, for my part, have eschewed both in favour of allocating capital to a proprietary trading firm, though whether that constitutes prudence or merely a different species of hubris remains, charitably, an open question.

clips.text_zh: Cramer話油價可能上150美金。CFD又爆倉區😭 真係又係學費。MACD睇緊，all-in就死。ok 繼續返工地盤。
clips.text_en_b1: Cramer posted on X saying oil at $150 is about to be reality. The /biz/ thread is reacting hard. Some anons say this is the setup to go long crude futures or energy CFDs. Others say it is a fake-out headline.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on Cramer tweet about oil hitting $150

signal.rationale: OP shares Cramer's bullish oil call at $150, thread sentiment leans long crude but with meme-tier conviction

clips.text_en_b2: Cramer dropped a post on X claiming that oil hitting 150 dollars a barrel is no longer some fringe fantasy but a near-term reality. The /biz/ thread is absolutely on fire, with some anons arguing this is the perfect setup to go long on crude futures, while others insist it is just another fake-out headline designed to lure retail traders into another CFD blow-up. MACD is flashing a cautious signal, so I am staying on the sidelines for now.
clips.text_en_c1: Cramer, never one to understate a directional thesis, recently took to X to declare that crude oil reaching the seemingly audacious level of $150 per barrel is no longer a hypothetical but an imminent reality. The reaction on /biz/ was immediate and visceral, with anons weighing whether to initiate long positions in crude futures or leveraged energy CFDs, while a more cautious contingent dismissed the proclamation as little more than headline-driven theatre. Having witnessed my own account obliterated on similar calls, I treat MACD divergence with the reverence it deserves before committing capital, lest a premature all-in prove terminal.
clips.text_en_c2: Cramer has once again taken to X to proclaim that crude at one hundred and fifty dollars per barrel is no longer a hypothetical tail risk but an imminent reality, sending the /biz/ thread into its customary state of apoplectic frenzy. The contingent advocating a long position in futures contracts or leveraged energy CFDs interprets the call as a generational entry point, while sceptics dismiss it as yet another headline-driven fake-out engineered to part retail traders from their margin. The MACD, as ever, is being scrutinised with quasi-religious intensity, and the consensus among the more battle-scarred participants is unambiguous: anyone contemplating an all-in position at this juncture is, to put it indelicately, consigning their capital to the bonfire. Back to the trading desk it is, then.

clips.text_zh: 今日做緊斜坡condition survey，soil nail design review，factor of safety要check返。日曬雨淋。Tommy叫我順便睇埋drainage，真係多嘢做😩 考牌都未溫完書。
clips.text_en_b1: On site today doing a slope condition survey and checking the soil nailing design. Factor of safety needs to be verified before sign-off. Tommy also asked me to review the drainage layout at the same time. It is a lot of work for one day.
clips.source_hint: General civil engineering context tied to OP's site-day frustration
clips.text_en_b2: On site today grinding through a slope condition survey while simultaneously reviewing the soil nailing design, and the factor of safety still needs a thorough cross-check before I can sign anything off. Although the work itself is pretty routine, Tommy has piled on extra tasks by asking me to take a look at the drainage layout as well, which means I am basically juggling two jobs at once. Pouring rain, blazing sun, and my FE exam revision is still gathering dust on the desk.
clips.text_en_c1: On site today conducting a comprehensive slope condition survey, with a concurrent soil nailing design review awaiting my attention. The factor of safety calculations, which must demonstrably exceed the stipulated threshold prior to formal sign-off, demand meticulous cross-referencing against the geotechnical report. Tommy, evidently operating under the assumption that my schedule permits lateral assignments, has also requested a drainage layout appraisal — a not-insubstantial addition to an already demanding itinerary. Under the punishing sun and intermittent rainfall, I find myself yearning for the sanctuary of an office, particularly given that my professional licensure examination preparation remains, embarrassingly, incomplete.
clips.text_en_c2: Spent the better part of the morning conducting a slope condition survey, methodically cataloguing superficial defects, measuring inclination gradients, and reviewing the soil nailing design against the geotechnical specifications. The factor of safety, that indispensable metric governing the margin between resisting and driving forces, requires thorough verification before any consultant can reasonably affix their signature to the submission. Tommy, with the serene optimism of a man unburdened by my deadlines, then requested—almost as an afterthought—that I audit the drainage layout as well, since, in his words, the storm drains have been 'looking a bit lively' after the recent downpours. The FE examination, meanwhile, remains an unopened chapter on my desk, taunting me with its unwavering indifference to the demands of fieldwork.

clips.text_zh: 返到office對住張beam-column layout圖，load path要行清楚，RC detail要check reinforcement同concrete cover。FE exam啱啱溫到這chapter lol。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: Sitting in the office checking a reinforced concrete beam and column layout. I need to follow the load path from slab to beam to column, then verify the steel reinforcement and concrete cover. It is exactly the kind of detail the FE exam asks about.
clips.source_hint: Structural RC check tied to FE exam revision

signal.rationale: Study and office work observation, no trade

clips.text_en_b2: Back at the office staring at a reinforced concrete beam-column layout, and I need to trace the load path carefully from slab right through to the foundation. The RC detailing itself looks alright, but the steel reinforcement spacing and concrete cover still need a meticulous review before I commit anything. It is funny because this exact chapter just happened to come up in my FE exam revision yesterday, so at least the theory is still fresh in my head.
clips.text_en_c1: Back at the office, I find myself engrossed in a reinforced concrete beam-and-column layout that warrants a methodical load-path verification — tracing tributary forces from slab through beam to column before any subsequent detailing can be deemed reliable. The reinforcement schedule and concrete cover specifications demand rigorous scrutiny, given that minor discrepancies in either parameter can precipitate disproportionately adverse structural consequences. Curiously, the chapter I had been revising for my Fundamentals of Engineering examination earlier that very day dovetailed precisely with these practical considerations, lending the theoretical preparation an immediate, tangible salience that I had not anticipated.
clips.text_en_c2: Back at the office and hunched over a reinforced concrete beam-column layout drawing whose linework suggests it was drafted in some bygone era of CAD orthodoxy. The load path—that is, the trajectory by which gravitational demands migrate from slab through beam to column and ultimately into the foundation—must be traced with deliberate care if one is to avoid the embarrassment of a detailing error surfacing at the most inopportune juncture. Reinforcement schedules demand verification against bending moment envelopes, and concrete cover requirements, often neglected until the resident engineer raises an eyebrow, must be cross-checked against the relevant code provisions. Curiously, the chapter I had been revising for the FE examination the previous evening addressed precisely this constellation of minutiae, a small mercy I shall not soon take for granted.

clips.text_zh: /g/有人問：仲有咩嘢係AI做唔到？ex-Meta researcher話AI已經可以摧毀成個國家。我個civil engineer job暫時安全，但white collar真係凍過水🧐 靠AI續命中。
clips.text_en_b1: An ex-Meta researcher posted on /g/ that OpenAI could already cripple the entire country by removing the alignment limits on its top models. Anons are asking what jobs humans can still do better than the newest AI. It is a scary thread to read at night.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on ex-Meta researcher warning about AI alignment
clips.text_en_b2: A former Meta researcher posted a pretty chilling take on /g/, arguing that if OpenAI stripped the alignment guardrails from its flagship models, the fallout could potentially cripple an entire nation overnight. Anons are now scrambling to figure out which white-collar professions still have any meaningful edge over the latest generation of AI. As a civil engineer, my job feels relatively safe for the moment, although I am quietly leaning on AI tools more and more to get through the day.
clips.text_en_c1: On /g/, an ex-Meta researcher has ignited a particularly unsettling discourse by suggesting that the most capable AI models, were their alignment constraints abruptly lifted, could already inflict systemic damage upon a nation's critical infrastructure. Anons, predictably, have pivoted to the question du jour: what remains of human economic value when artificial intelligence can ostensibly perform the preponderance of cognitive labour? As a civil engineer, my own employment prospects appear, for the moment, reasonably insulated — yet the broader white-collar erosion he describes scarcely permits complacency, and one suspects the reprieve may prove temporary.
clips.text_en_c2: A former Meta researcher, posting on /g/, has advanced the rather arresting proposition that OpenAI could, by simply relinquishing the alignment constraints currently imposed upon its most capable models, inflict crippling damage upon the nation's critical infrastructure. The thread that has ensued oscillates between existential alarm and sardonic resignation, with anons earnestly cataloguing those occupations—plumbing, electrical work, civil engineering, the trades generally—that remain, for the moment at least, beyond the reach of even the most sophisticated transformer architectures. White-collar cognitarians are, by contrast, contemplating their curricula vitae with mounting unease. I, however, derive no small comfort from the observation that reinforced concrete detailing continues to resist automation with admirable stubbornness, and shall continue to lean upon AI as a research adjunct rather than a career obituary.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信今日又whatsapp叫我去做gym。我自己80kg，bench 1 plate，squat 90kg，deadlift 120kg。flat到睇唔出有muscle😩 應該cut定繼續bulk？wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: An anon on /fit/ asks how to know when he has bulked enough to cut. He went from 83kg fat, cut to 65kg skinnyfat, then lean bulked back to 80kg. His lifts now are bench 3x8 at one plate, squat 3x6 at 90kg, deadlift 3x8 at 120kg. He still looks flat.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread about when to stop bulking and start cutting
clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /fit/ is stuck in that classic bulk-or-cut dilemma and wants a clear signal on when he has finally piled on enough muscle to start cutting. His journey so far has been a rollercoaster: he kicked off at 83 kilos and fairly overweight, then cut all the way down to a skinnyfat 65, before lean bulking his way back up to a solid 80.
clips.text_en_c1: On /fit/, an anon posed the eternally vexing question of how one ought to determine when a bulk has sufficiently concluded and a cut ought to commence. His trajectory is instructive: an initial 83 kilograms of what might charitably be termed adipose tissue preceded an aggressive cut to a rather gaunt 65 kilograms, after which a methodical lean bulk restored him to his present 80 kilograms. His current lifts — a bench press of one plate for three sets of eight, a squat of 90 kilograms across three sets of six, and a deadlift of 120 kilograms for three sets of eight — suggest respectable strength, yet aesthetically he remains,…
clips.text_en_c2: The /fit/ thread poses the eternal quandary of the intermediate lifter: how does one ascertain, with any reasonable confidence, the optimal juncture at which a lean bulk ought to yield to a cutting phase? The poster in question embarked upon his journey at a somewhat rotund eighty-three kilograms, endured the requisite caloric penance to arrive at a rather gaunt sixty-five, and has subsequently lean-bulked his way back to a presentable eighty. His current lifts—a bench press of one plate for three sets of eight, a squat of ninety kilograms for three sets of six, and a deadlift of one hundred and twenty kilograms for three sets of eight—suggest commendable adherence to progressive overload.

clips.text_zh: 返到屋企一個人，又開Netflix睇動漫。睇下Soremachi同朋友嘅新一集lol。30歲仲睇動漫，廢柴確認。但開心lol。👍
clips.text_en_b1: Ishiguro ranked his favourite characters from his own manga Soremachi and drew them in swimsuits. He also talked about random stuff, like how Ebi-chan is based on his first crush from elementary school. It is a nice chill thread for late night on /a/.
clips.source_hint: /a/ thread on Soremachi author ranking his own characters
clips.text_en_b2: Got home from a long day, kicked off my shoes, and ended up alone on the couch with Netflix queued up and Soremachi lined up for a late-night session. Caught the newest episode with a friend and honestly had a proper laugh at the absurd character interactions. Turning thirty and still binging anime pretty much every weekend, so I have officially confirmed the full-on degenerate lifestyle at this point.
clips.text_en_c1: Returning home to an uncharacteristically quiet apartment, I surrendered once again to the comforting predictability of Netflix and the latest episode of Soremachi, that wistful chronicle of friendships forged and frayed. Ishiguro, the author, had taken to /a/ to rank his favourite characters from the very series he had created, rendering them in swimsuits with an evident affection, whilst regaling readers with ancillary reminiscences — notably that Ebi-chan owes her existence to his formative crush from elementary school. At thirty, indulging in such fare might constitute confirmation of terminal underachievement, yet the unalloyed pleasure it bestows remains, I would argue, beyond rational dispute.
clips.text_en_c2: Ishiguro, in a manifestation of authorial indulgence that can only be described as endearingly self-congratulatory, has elected to rank his favoured characters from his own manga Soremachi and subsequently render them in swimsuits, an exercise that has occasioned no small measure of affectionate bemusement within the /a/ thread. He also meanders, with characteristic nonchalance, through a variety of ostensibly tangential observations, including the disclosure that the character Ebi-chan was modelled, with what one assumes is a mixture of nostalgia and mild embarrassment, upon his very first infatuation during the elementary school years. For those of us navigating the twilight hours between productivity and sleep, the thread functions as a delightful palate cleanser, a reminder that creators occasionally possess the capacity to be simultaneously insufferable and thoroughly charming in roughly equal measure.
